2.3 Advertising 
 
A licensed or registered person should ensure that invitations and 
advertisements  do not contain information  that is false, disparaging, 
misleading or deceptive.

Licensed or re gistered persons should note the various Schedules to the 
Code. These are part of the Code and provide, among other things, 
supplemental  materials  such as risk disclosure  statements.

Unless otherwise  specified  or the context otherwise  requires, words and 
phrases in the Code shall be interpreted  by reference  to any definition of 
such word or phrase in Part 1 of Schedule 1 to the SFO.

This Code does not have the force of law and should not be interpreted  in a 
way that would override the provision of any law.

(a) A licensed or registered  person should, as part of the know 
your client procedures, assess the client’s knowledge of 
derivatives and characterize the client based on his 
knowledge of derivatives.

(b) Where a client without knowledge  of derivatives  wishes to 
purchase a derivative product (he reafter refer to as a 
“transaction” in this paragraph) which is:  
 
(i) traded on an exchange and the licensed or registered 
person has not solicited the client or made a 
recommendation  to the client in relation to the proposed 
transaction, the licensed or regis tered person should 
explain the relevant  risks associated  with the product to 
the client;

missing_premises: Product classification: the selected product family and its contractual terms, payoff, underlying exposures and trading arrangements are absent. No supplied selection provides the complete structured-product definition, inclusions, exclusions or its relationship to derivative-product and complex-product classifications.

Complete authority: the required product-family circular and substantive FAQ answers have not been supplied. The gifts FAQ HTML selections principally contain navigation and a truncated answer ending; the original FAQ PDF has no selected text. These do not establish any product-specific advertising or gifts rule.

Incorporated provisions: the full relevant statutory definitions, Code application provisions, Schedules and cross-referenced requirements are missing. A table-of-contents entry identifies a provision but does not establish its operative content.

Advertising branches: paragraph 2.3 supports the general content standard, but the supplied selections do not settle product-specific scope, authorization requirements, exclusions, exemptions, warnings, disclosures or conditions for particular recipients and distribution channels.

Client and transaction branches: the supplied text shows a derivatives-knowledge assessment and one exchange-traded, unsolicited transaction branch. The non-exchange branch is truncated, and the full suitability, complex-product and professional-investor provisions and their exceptions are not supplied.

Temporal applicability: the relevant conduct date and authoritative evidence of which circular, FAQ and incorporated provisions applied at that time are missing. Different printed revision dates in the selections do not resolve this.

Institutional applicability: no evidence establishes the relevant entity’s licensing or registration, regulated role, issuer or distributor capacity, exchange participation, or any applicable exemption or waiver.

Operational applicability: no product offering documents, actual advertisements, distribution records, solicitation or recommendation records, client categorization records, or supporting exemption assessments are supplied.

Source completeness: substantial text remains unselected. The JFIU selections concern suspicious transaction reporting and do not establish structured-product classification or advertising requirements. No exhaustive branch inventory can be supported from the supplied material.
next_source_questions: Which exact product family and conduct date are being assessed? Supply the final product terms and offering documents, together with the relevant advertising materials and intended recipient and distribution-channel details.

Supply the complete official circular and FAQ for that product family, including their titles, annexes, footnotes, linked incorporated provisions, scope clauses, exceptions and authoritative amendment or supersession information. Their exact identities are not established by the supplied selections.

Supply the complete applicable Part 1 of Schedule 1 to the SFO provisions needed to determine structured-product classification, including all relevant definitions, inclusions, exclusions and cross-references.

Supply the complete official statutory and product-specific provisions governing invitations and advertisements for the selected family, including authorization, exemption, warning and disclosure branches and the conditions attached to each.

Supply the full Code interpretation and application provisions, paragraph 2.3 with any associated notes, paragraph 5.1A including the truncated non-exchange branch, paragraphs 5.2 and 5.3, the applicable complex-product provisions, and paragraphs 15.1 through 15.5 with their incorporated requirements.

If promotion using gifts is within scope, supply the full operative paragraph 3.11 and the substantive questions and answers from the listed gifts FAQ sources, including their scope and exceptions; navigation labels and the truncated answer ending are insufficient.

Supply institutional records establishing the intermediary’s relevant status and role, and operational records establishing client classification, derivatives knowledge, solicitation or recommendation, and satisfaction of any claimed exemption conditions.

Once those materials are supplied, can each classification, advertising, client, transaction and exception branch be mapped to a complete operative quotation and the facts triggering it? Preserve the complete source text and its version information before freezing the branch inventory or coding; hashes alone cannot satisfy that closure test.
value.proposition: The supplied selections establish a general advertising provision, but do not establish full structured-product classification or the complete related advertising regime. Express provision: paragraph 2.3 states that a licensed or registered person should ensure that invitations and advertisements contain no false, disparaging, misleading or deceptive information. The Code also expressly incorporates its Schedules, generally refers undefined words and phrases to Part 1 of Schedule 1 to the SFO, and states that it does not have the force of law or override law. Paragraph 5.1A expressly requires assessment of clients’ derivatives knowledge and supplies one conditional branch concerning exchange-traded derivative products; the supplied selection truncates the next branch. Inference: these provisions identify relevant questions for further examination, but neither classify the selected product family nor establish that structured products, derivative products and complex products are interchangeable categories. Assumptions: this proposal assesses only the supplied selections; the selected product’s terms, relevant conduct date, intermediary status and intended recipients remain unspecified. File names, hashes, publication and possession of a document are not evidence of applicability or completeness. The retained question remains open: the complete source slice cannot yet be frozen, and every applicable branch cannot yet be enumerated before coding.
